model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between ACC (%) and the Co-occurrence Number, displaying five distinct methods—Base, MEND, FT, IKE, and ROME—each represented by a different colored line with unique markers. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10^3, with tick marks at intervals of 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 40 to 65. The “Base” method is shown as a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 39% ACC at a Co-occurrence Number of 0 and increasing slightly to about 44% at 10^3. The “MEND” method is depicted with brown diamond markers, beginning at around 44% ACC and rising to approximately 56% at 10^3. The “FT” method, marked with blue triangles, starts at about 40% ACC and increases to roughly 47% at 10^3. The “IKE” method, indicated by red triangles, begins at approximately 43% ACC and rises to about 49% at 10^3. The “ROME” method, shown with green squares, starts at about 51% ACC and increases steadily to approximately 66% at 10^3.
